title: THE LAW SET BEFORE THE PEOPLE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the law Moses set before the Israelites. These are the stipulations, decrees and laws Moses gave them when they came out of Egypt and were in the valley near Beth Peor east of the Jordan, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon and was defeated by Moses and the Israelites as they came out of Egypt. They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan. This land extended from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge to Mount Sirion (that is, Hermon), and included all the Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah. - Deut 4:44-49 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This passage forms a bridge, closing Moses' opening addresses and setting the stage for the detailed laws to come. It records the setting — the valley near Beth Peor, in the land recently won from Sihon and Og — and notes that this is "the law Moses set before the Israelites." Everything that follows in Deuteronomy would be the unfolding of God's covenant instruction for His people. The stage is set for God's word to be laid out in full.

There is something worth noticing in the simple phrase "set before the Israelites." God's law was placed before the people, laid out openly for them to hear, understand, and follow. God did not hide His will or make it inaccessible. He set it plainly before His people so they could know how to live in relationship with Him. God is a God who reveals, who makes His ways known.

We are richly blessed to have God's word set before us. Unlike those who grope in the dark, wondering how to please God, we have His revealed word, clear and accessible. The Scriptures set before us the knowledge of God, the way of salvation, and the path of life. This is a gift beyond measure.

The mention of the victories over Sihon and Og reminds us that God's word comes to us grounded in His faithful acts in history. The God who speaks is the God who acts, who kept His promises and gave His people victory. And the whole of Scripture, set before us, ultimately points to Christ, the living Word (John 1:1). As we prepare to hear God's law unfold in the chapters ahead, let us receive His word with reverence and joy, treasuring the God who sets His truth plainly before us and leads us to life in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treasure the gift of having God's word set plainly before you?
2. How does knowing the God who speaks is also the God who acts strengthen your trust?
3. How does all of Scripture point you to Christ, the living Word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for setting Your word plainly before me, revealing Your ways and the path of life. Help me to receive Your truth with reverence and joy, treasuring the Scriptures that lead me to Christ, the living Word. Amen.
